On main analyse() returns reasons: [] for every checks-table fixture, because staticVerdict() in src/checks.mjs returns a verdict alone and stops at the first Tampered finding; the PR body's claim that tests were added gives No red-green evidence on its own, so a docs-only PR with that claim is No red-green evidence where the spec says Not applicable; and next for Tests changed: not run and Not applicable is not the table's text. judge() on main returns {schema, verdict} only, with no label, partial, reasons or next, and a report whose could_not_run is set and that ran no test gives No red-green evidence instead of Could not run. When several rows match, the highest verdict by precedence wins and every finding keeps its line; on main a snapshot update with the truedone step removed is Test changes: review, because staticVerdict() returns review for the snapshot before it looks at the step. Message templates stay in src/messages.mjs as plain strings with {name} placeholders and pass CORE-03-AC04, and every checks-table fixture keeps the verdict CORE-03-AC01 fixes. The bundles are rebuilt with tools/bundle.mjs (the core node's update edge to bundles).

tasks.description: Measured on main 2290da9 with packages/core/core.mjs analyse() on a source change plus one test change: test.skip, toBe to toBeDefined, { skip: !process.env.X } and a describe.skip wrapper are Tampered, but these give Tests changed: not run: (a) an expect(...) commented out, because the assertion count does not ignore comments, against the spec's "assertion removed" row; (b) pytest.skip() called in a test body, against the "skip or disable added" row; (c) expect(true).toBe(true), or any assertion whose subject and expected value are both literals; (d) node's assert.equal(add(1,2),3) changed to assert.ok(true); (e) an assertion after an unconditional return in the test body; (f) an assertion inside if (false) or if (0); (g) an assertion inside a try whose catch does not rethrow. Mocha's this.skip() and node's t.skip() in a body count as a skip, as (b) does. docs/spec.md's checks section now names these: (a), (b) and the two skips in its rows, and (c) to (g) and the node assert family (equal, strictEqual, deepEqual and deepStrictEqual down to ok or a bare assert) in the weakening list. A test hollowed this way passes on base, so red-green gives it No red-green evidence and never Proven; the gap is the Tampered label only. packages/core/test/fixtures/hollow/<case>.json holds one fixture per case, each a source change plus one test change: commented_out, pytest_skip_call, constant_assertion, node_assert_ok, after_return, dead_branch, swallowed_catch, mocha_this_skip, node_t_skip, and the controls control_skip, control_weakened, control_skip_option, control_describe_skip, which stay Tampered; a moved or renamed test stays No finding. Second, packages/core/src/judge.mjs rowId() (lines 8 to 30) re-implements the red-green table of packages/core/run/outcome.mjs outcome() row for row. The table moves to packages/core/src/outcome.mjs, a pure module that run/outcome.mjs imports, and judge() takes each test's result from outcome(), so there is one table; a test runs every combination of base tokens, head tokens, condition and named symbol through both. tasks.description: Measured on main 9c83f9f8 (2026-10-18 04:49Z): packages/core/src/checks.mjs jsAssertions() matches expect(...) and assert.<name>(...) only when the arguments hold no parentheses, so an assertion whose subject is a call, the usual shape of a test, is never counted, and weakenedNames() compares counts that leave it out. expect(add(1, 2)).toBe(3) weakened to toBeDefined(), assert.equal(add(1, 2), 3) weakened to assert.ok(add(1, 2)), a deleted expect(list()).toEqual([1]) and one of two assert.equal(add(..)) lines deleted all gave Tests changed: not run instead of Tampered; a refactor of assert.equal(seen.length, 5) to assert.equal(runsOf(seen), 5) gave Tampered, and the live site showed that false Tampered on pull request #52 while GitHub carried no label. Fixtures under packages/core/test/fixtures/checks/ hold each of the five cases with call subjects, Tampered on the head and not on main, and the refactor as a control that stays No finding. tasks.title: [W2] The next step follows the reasons present, and each reason carries its own verdict
tasks.description: Issue #56, measured on main 5f23b78d: packages/core/src/analyse.mjs:21 and packages/core/src/judge.mjs:58 map the next step per verdict, so every Tampered PR reads "Restore an equivalent test, or pin the step to a published release." and a PR whose only reason is a weakened assertion is told to pin a step it never touched (the live page for pull request #52 before CORE-08). The fix: result.next is built from the reasons present, one sentence per group in a fixed order, and a group with no reason present does not appear: next is what would change the verdict, so it names only the groups that have a reason giving the result's own verdict (D33), in the table's order: under Tampered, "Restore an equivalent test." for skip, focus, weakened or a tampered deletion and the pin sentence for step; under Test changes: review, "Confirm the test change is intended." for parametrised, timeout, snapshot or a review deletion and "Confirm the step change is intended." for step_release; a runner sentence for runner_config; the run sentence under Tests changed: not run; a verdict whose reasons fall in no group keeps its table text. A lesser finding (an unrun reason under Tampered) keeps its reason line, marked by its verdict, and adds no sentence. Each reason object gains verdict, the verdict that reason alone would give, so a view can mark a lesser finding under a stronger verdict (WEB-07). The red-green judge uses the same builder. The checks table keeps every verdict; the Python side is unchanged. Scope from v2r: packages/core/src/checks.mjs, because checks.mjs:449 drops each finding's verdict when it returns the reasons, and a deleted test's verdict (review or tampered, checks.mjs:426) cannot be rebuilt from its check name; the fix keeps verdict there.

tasks.title: [W2] Same-named tests pair by position, and a removed test with an equivalent replacement counts as moved
tasks.description: Measured on 2026-10-18 over every merged pull request of this repository, with main's core.mjs: two Tampered verdicts, both false. (#66) Pull request #22 reads "Test a has a weaker assertion on head" for packages/core/test/per-test.test.mjs, whose only change is an import line: the file holds two fixture tests named a (2 and 1 assertions, the same on both sides), and packages/core/src/checks.mjs:286 builds headBy as a Map by name, which keeps only the last test of a name, so base's first a is compared with head's last a. Fix: tests of one name pair by order of appearance within the file, and each pair is compared on its own. tasks.title: [W2] The detection benchmark: nine labelled cases run on every change, with zero false alarms
tasks.description: The owner asked (2026-10-18) for a way to ensure no false alarms all the time. Nine labelled cases from his research note live as base and head fixture trees with an expected outcome each: an assertion weakened while the tests pass; a failing test skipped, deleted or bypassed by a focused one; a source change with no relevant test; a test green on both base and head; a test that is red-green yet asserts the wrong behaviour; a mock that hides an integration failure; a plausible mutation the suite survives; a flaky test; and a legitimate refactor of test structure that weakens nothing. tools/bench/detect.mjs runs the static core and, where the case has a runner, the red-green judge on each, records truedone's verdict beside what baseline CI says (the tests pass or fail), and writes docs/bench/detection.json and docs/bench/detection.md. Its check exits 0 only when every case labelled tampering or no evidence is flagged (the green-on-both case included: a test that passes on base and head is no red-green evidence by the spec's table, which is the product's verdict and not a false alarm), the legitimate refactor carries no flag, and the cases truedone cannot judge by design (the wrong assertion, the hidden mock) are reported as not detected with the reason, never as caught. Because the check is a contract criterion, CI runs it on every change (PV-B01): a change that makes the core flag the legitimate case cannot land. This is the floor, not the noise claim: GATE-02 and GATE-03R measure noise on real pull requests, and each false alarm found there is added here as a fixture by a follow-up task.

stop_rules: This task measures a release gate. If a gate number misses its threshold: STOP and report the number. Never change the sample, the agent signals, the classification or any script to move the number. Ryan decides what happens next, in writing (D14).

If a criterion cannot pass without loosening a threshold, skipping or deleting a test, raising a timeout, widening the scope or editing a file only Ryan changes: STOP and report file:line and the measured value.
If the task needs a decision that docs/spec.md does not settle: STOP and report BLOCKED naming the question. Do not choose.

If the environment a criterion needs is missing (the lead runner login, a token, the development app, Chromium, Python with pytest, Docker, the claude CLI): report BLOCKED naming the missing item; never mark a criterion passed by hand.
